claims.text: NVIDIA's own newsroom post says only that "NVIDIA has additionally made an investment in SSI" — no dollar figure, no equity percentage, no term sheet detail
Ilya Sutskever, SSI's CEO, is quoted saying "NVIDIA is making a substantial investment in SSI that will let us 10x our compute in the next 12 months"
Jensen Huang's line: "Ilya has pioneered fundamental breakthroughs at the foundation of modern AI, beginning with AlexNet"
Bloomberg published it first, sourced to "people familiar with the matter" — not a filing, not a company statement
Reuters ... corroborated the same $5 billion independently ... the deal is described as an "equity investment" paired with Vera Rubin hardware access
TechCrunch ... hedges further, with a source describing the investment only as one that "stretches into multiple billions"
TechCrunch notes NVIDIA was already an investor via SSI's 2025 round, reported at roughly $2 billion raised against a $32 billion valuation
NVIDIA's framing of the deal claims SSI "has achieved significant research milestones"
the company raised a $1B seed round at a $5B post-money valuation, backed by SV Angel, DST Global, Sequoia Capital, and Andreessen Horowitz
an approximately $2B raise at a $32B valuation, led by Greenoaks Capital (~$500M) alongside returning backers Andreessen Horowitz and DST Global, plus new entrant Lightspeed Venture Partners
CB Insights' company profile tracks only $3B in disclosed equity ($1B seed plus the $2B 2025 round)
Reuters' coverage of the April 2025 round confirms that both Alphabet/Google and NVIDIA participated in that $32B raise
SSI was founded in June 2024 — not 2023 — a detail worth correcting since it changes the company's age at deal time
SSI stated its mission in one sentence: "We will pursue safe superintelligence in a straight shot, with one focus, one goal, and one product"
A detailed independent critique ... disputes a load-bearing premise — that LLMs generalize worse than humans do — flatly countering that "humans do not actually generalize all that well"
the board's official statement said Altman "was not consistently candid in his communications with the board, hindering its ability to exercise its responsibilities"

more than 700 of OpenAI's roughly 770 staff signed an open letter threatening to resign ... Satya Nadella announced Altman and Greg Brockman "will be joining Microsoft to lead a new advanced AI research team"

in October 2025 testimony in Musk v. OpenAI, Sutskever said he had considered removing Altman for "at least a year" before the vote and had authored an internal memo accusing him of "a consistent pattern of lying"
Meta instead hired SSI co-founder Daniel Gross ... Sutskever's internal note called Gross's time at SSI "winding down" and said he was "grateful for his early contributions"
Sutskever's on-record response downplayed the episode: "We are flattered by their attention but are focused on seeing our work through. We have the compute, we have the team, and we know what to do"

Responding directly to Michael Burry's circular-financing and Enron comparisons, the company sent Wall Street analysts a seven-page memo putting strategic investments at $4.7 billion year-to-date and $3.7 billion in a single quarter — about 7% of that quarter's revenue
Jensen Huang was already walking the framing back: "It was never a commitment... we were very happy and honored that they invited us, but we will invest one step at a time"
What actually closed, inside OpenAI's larger $122 billion round in March 2026, was a direct equity stake of roughly $30 billion — with no gigawatt-deployment conditionality attached
Q1 FY2027 revenue ran $81.6 billion, with $58.3 billion in GAAP net income and $50.3 billion of operating cash flow

SemiAnalysis's technical accounting puts Google's TPUv7 at roughly 20-50% lower total cost per useful FLOP than NVIDIA's GB200/GB300 — around 30% lower than GB200 specifically ... Anthropic reportedly runs on the order of 400K purchased TPUv7 units plus 600K rented from Google
Vera Rubin — Blackwell's successor, 336 billion transistors, roughly 3.5x Blackwell's training FLOPS via a new Vera CPU replacing Grace — entered full production June 1, 2026
Anthropic's headline $47B figure is exactly that: its most recent monthly revenue, annualized
Independent analysis puts Anthropic's actual calendar-2026 revenue at $20-26B — nearly half the run-rate headline — and its FY2025 actual revenue at just $10B
OpenAI shows the same pattern at smaller scale: a ~$25B annualized run-rate by early 2026 sat alongside $13.1B in FY2025 actual booked revenue and roughly $5.7B in Q1 2026 actual revenue
xAI's $3.2B figure is unusually reliable for this set: it comes from a SpaceX-merger IPO filing ... alongside a disclosed $6.4B operating loss

NVIDIA shares fell as much as 5.3% intraday and closed down 5.09% the same day the deal was announced, but reporting attributes that move mainly to a broader semiconductor and China-chip-competition selloff
Polymarket's "AI bubble burst by...?" contract ... was pricing roughly 18% Yes against 82% No on $2.91M of volume as of July 28, 2026
Josh Wolfe of Lux Capital frames the gap in dollar terms, estimating frontier AI labs need somewhere between $250-400B of additional realized economic value to justify valuations already on the books

the Bank for International Settlements, whose annual report warned that disappointing AI returns could turn hyperscaler capex — over $1T combined across the top five in 2025-2026, funded partly by $159B in tech corporate bond issuance in just five months of 2026 — into a "protracted investment bust"
DeepMind ran roughly a decade from its 2010 founding to its first reported profit (£43.8M / $59.6M in 2020), and needed a mid-journey de-risking event — Google's roughly $500M acquisition in 2014
OpenAI's runway was shorter, about 4.5 years from its no-product, no-revenue December 2015 founding to its first monetized product, the GPT-3 API beta in June 2020
Sutskever reversed course publicly the same day (X post: "I deeply regret my participation in the board's actions...")
